silabus_tekst: RNU study course “Latvian for Foreigners” description Study program Information Systems Amount 6 CP = 150 ac.h. Author (s) Sandra Plota Preliminary knowledge, Related study courses No preliminary knowledge required Aim To provide students the basic knowledge and develop their competence to communicate in the Latvian language in professional and everyday situations at basic level. Planned Learning Outcomes (PLO) Ability to maintain communication on the everyday situations topics in the Latvian language on the basic level. Ability to analyze, systematize, synthesize and integrate information necessary for the operation of an enterprise. Ability to exchange information directly on the basic level of Latvian knowledge. Ability to use the acquired knowledge in the bounds of professional activities. Literature and other sources of information: Compulsory reading Auziņa, I., Berķe, M., Lazareva, A., Šalme, A. A1 Laipa. Latviešu valoda. Mācību grāmata. Rīga: LVA, 2022. Lazareva, A., Šalme, A. A1 Laipa. Latviešu valoda. Darba burtnīca. Rīga: LVA, 2022. Recommended - "Es protu latviešu valodu", Polikāns Kaspars, Zvaigzne ABC, 2017 Māci un mācies latviešu valodu - http://maciunmacies.valoda.lv/valodas-apguve/e-nodarbibas#tab2 Sāksim runāt latviski http://maciunmacies.valoda.lv/images/speles/ LVA_Saksim_runat_latviski/index.html Languagehelpers https://www.languagehelpers.com the Latvian Language Helper Study course content and schedule of contact hours Week Topic Academic hours 1 Iepazīšanās 4 2 Adrese 4 3 Ģimene 4 1. 2. 3. 4. • • • • • • • 4 Dzīvesvieta 4 5 Pilsēta 4 6 Ikdiena 4 7 Ēdienreizes 4 8 Group work:"Mana pilsēta" 4 9 Laika apstākļi 4 10 Iepirkšanas 4 11 Kafejnīcā un restorānā 4 12 Veselība 4 13 Brīvais laiks 4 14 Ceļošana 4 15 Svētki 4 16 Iepazīšanās 4 Total: 64 ac.h Description of students’ self-studies organization and assignments Self-study work Description Planned Learning Outcomes (PLO) % of final evaluation Students are required to study the indicated compulsory reading, sources, and methodological materials, as they are essential for understanding the fundamental concepts, completing assignments, and successfully mastering the course content. Detailed descriptions of each independent task and the assessment system are provided in the e-learning environment. Grammar test 1 Testing knowledge and skills in alfabets, divskaņi, lietvārds, īpašības vārds, vietniekvārds. Students demonstrate knowledge and skills in basic Latvian grammar elements including alphabet, diphthongs, nouns, adjectives, pronouns (PLO 1, 3). 12% Grammar test 2 Testing knowledge and skills in skaitļi, kalendārs, skaitļa vārds, apstākļa vārds, darbības vārds, prievārds. Students demonstrate knowledge and skills in numbers, calendar, numerals, adverbs, verbs, prepositions (PLO 1, 3). 12% Speaking test 1 Speaking on the topics mastered in the framework of the study course: Iepazīšanās, Adrese, Ģimene, Dzīvesvieta, Pilsēta, Ikdiena, Ēdienreizes. Students demonstrate competences in speaking on introductory, address, family, residence, city, daily routine, meals topics (PLO 1, 3). 12% Speaking test 2 Speaking on the topics mastered in the framework of the study course: Laika apstākļi, Iepirkšanās, Kafeinīcā un restorānā, Veselība, Brīvais laiks, Ceļošana, Svētki. Students demonstrate competences in speaking on weather, shopping, cafe/restaurant, health, free time, travel, holidays topics (PLO 1, 3, 4). 12% Group work "Mana pilsēta" Skills to communicate within related topic, know vocabulary about related topic, competent to use appropriate phrases to design own text. Students demonstrate knowledge, competences, and skills in communicating about city topics, using appropriate vocabulary and phrases (PLO 1, 2, 3, 4). 17% Final test Comprehensive test covering all course content. Students synthesize all acquired knowledge, skills, and competences in Latvian language communication (PLO 1, 2, 3, 4). 35% Evaluation of mastering the study course Level Requirements Very high (10 –with distinction 9 – excellent) 10 (with distinction) - Knowledge, skills and competences exceed the requirements of the study course and demonstrate the ability to perform independent research as well as the deep understanding of problems. 9 (excellent) - Knowledge, skills and competences fully meet the requirements of the study course, student is able to apply the acquired knowledge independently. High (8 –very good 7 - good) 8 (very good) – The requirements of the study course are fully met, however, there is insufficient understanding of individual issues to use the knowledge independently for the solution of more complex problems. 7 (good) – The requirements of the study course are met in general, however, sometimes the inability to use the acquired knowledge independently is detected. Average (6 – almost good 5 – satisfactory 4 –almost satisfactory) 6 (almost good) – The requirements of the study course are met in general, however insufficient understanding of some problems and inability to apply the acquired knowledge is detected. 5 (satisfactory) – The requirements of the study course are met for the most part, however insufficient understanding of many problems and inability to apply the acquired knowledge is detected. 4 (almost satisfactory) – The requirements of the study course are met, for the most part, however insufficient understanding of some main concepts is detected as well as considerable difficulties in the practical application of the acquired knowledge are stated. Low (3 – 1 – negative evaluation) 3 (bad) – Knowledge is superficial and incomplete; the student is unable to use it in specific situations, 2 (very bad) – Superficial and incomplete knowledge of only some problems, the most part of the study course is not mastered. 1 (very very bad) – An absence of understanding of the main problems of the subject matter, almost no knowledge of the content of the study course.
